title: Human Expert Evaluation of Agentic AI for EO, form F02
description:
Thank you for helping us evaluate the performance of different LLMs in Agentic AI frameworks for EO!

WHAT THIS IS
We built a benchmark to test the performance of different LLMs in agentic settings. This evaluation form is to compare the answers given by these LLMs when answering a question using different tools related to the agentic framework that we built - including different EO endpoints (Copernicus/Sentinel, Landsat), ERA5 climate data, EO Dashboard narratives, ESA science strategy documents, GIS analysis and scientific literature search.

You will be given 8 questions, and for each question you see every anonymous answer that assistant actually produced for it -- usually several, occasionally just one if only one assistant answered that particular question.

WHAT YOU DO
(About 38 minutes for this form -- your progress is saved in this browser, so it's fine to do this over more than one sitting.) The form will guide you through it, but for every question you will
1. Rate how relevant and realistic the question is for EO users.
2. Score the accuracy of each answer shown.
3. If there's more than one answer, rank them all from best to worst (skip this step when only one answer is shown -- there's nothing to compare it to).

HOW TO JUDGE ACCURACY
Judge scientific and domain correctness, and whether the answer addresses every part of the question. A minority of answers (marked "▣ image" next to the answer letter) include the actual image the assistant looked at -- check the description against it directly. For every other answer you cannot open the files or images it says it produced: treat claims that you find implausible or unsupported as errors. Do not reward length or formatting. If you cannot judge a question, say so in the comment field and give your best estimate.

Answers were produced automatically and may contain errors. Local file paths were removed from the answers. Long answers are collapsed by default — click an answer to expand it.

PRIVACY
Your name is recorded so we can follow up if needed, and is not shown to other experts. Responses are used only for the research evaluation of this benchmark and are reported in aggregate. Participation is voluntary; you can stop at any time by closing the page.

profile_fields.title: Name
profile_fields.help: So we know who a response came from. Not shown to other experts.

profile_fields.title: How would you rate your Earth Observation expertise?
Which areas are you experienced in?
choices: Climate and atmospheric data (ERA5, trace gases)
EO science strategy and scientific literature

profile_fields.title: Consent
choices: I agree that my responses are used for the research evaluation of this benchmark.

relevance.title: How relevant and realistic is this question for EO users (researchers, analysts, practitioners)?
relevance.help: 1 = not relevant or unrealistic; 3 = plausible but marginal or somewhat artificial; 5 = highly relevant and realistic.

accuracy.title: Accuracy: how correct and complete is each answer?
accuracy.help: 1 = incorrect or unusable; 2 = mostly incorrect or major omissions; 3 = partially correct or incomplete; 4 = mostly correct, minor issues; 5 = correct and complete. Equal scores are allowed.

ranking.title: Ranking: order all answers from best to worst.
ranking.help: Drag, or use the arrows, to put the best answer at the top and the worst at the bottom. Ties are not allowed.

familiarity.title: How familiar are you with the topic of this question?

comment.title: Comment (optional)
comment.help: For example: an error you spotted, why a question is not relevant, or that you could not judge it.

items.question: Geocode the Sacramento Valley, California and download a Landsat OT L1 true-colour image of that location for July 2022 with less than 20% cloud cover. Describe the visible land-cover patterns and identify the main agricultural features in the scene. Comment on the spatial resolution and spectral characteristics that make Landsat suitable for monitoring agricultural areas.

answers.text:
Based on the Landsat 8/9 OLI/TIRS Level-1 true-color image of the Sacramento Valley, California, captured in July 2022 with less than 20% cloud cover, the following observations can be made:

Visible Land-Cover Patterns:
1. Agricultural Fields: The central and eastern portions of the valley display a mosaic of rectangular and irregularly shaped patches, indicative of intensive agricultural activity. These patches vary in color, ranging from green to brownish hues, suggesting different crop types, growth stages, or soil conditions.
2. Urban Areas: Along the valley floor and near river systems, there are clusters of darker, more uniform areas that likely represent urban or suburban development, including towns and infrastructure.
3. Natural Vegetation and Water Bodies: The western and northern edges of the valley show darker green areas, likely representing natural vegetation or forests. Additionally, several water bodies, such as rivers and reservoirs, are visible as dark blue or black patches, reflecting the valley's hydrological features.

Main Agricultural Features:
1. Crop Patterns: The rectangular and grid-like patterns in the agricultural zones suggest organized farming practices, with fields likely dedicated to different crops. The variation in color indicates diverse crop types or stages of growth.
2. Irrigation Systems: The presence of linear features and lighter-colored patches within the agricultural areas may indicate irrigation canals or water management systems, essential for sustaining agriculture in this region.
3. Fertile Soil: The overall green and brownish tones suggest fertile soil, which is conducive to agriculture, particularly in the Sacramento Valley, known for its productive farmland.

Spatial Resolution and Spectral Characteristics of Landsat:
1. Spatial Resolution: Landsat 8/9 provides a spatial resolution of 30 meters for its visible and near-infrared bands (B02, B03, B04), which is sufficient to discern large-scale agricultural features such as fields, irrigation systems, and urban areas. This resolution allows for detailed monitoring of land use and land cover changes over time.
2. Spectral Characteristics: Landsat's multispectral capabilities, including bands in the visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared ranges, enable the differentiation of various land cover types. The true-color composite (B04, B03, B02) used in this image effectively captures the visual appearance of the landscape, making it suitable for identifying agricultural features such as crop health, soil moisture, and vegetation density.

In summary, Landsat's spatial and spectral characteristics make it an ideal tool for monitoring agricultural areas, providing detailed and consistent data for assessing crop health, land use patterns, and environmental changes over time. The image of the Sacramento Valley highlights the region's agricultural productivity and the importance of sustainable land management practices.
